stem:
Priya slides a steel tiffin box across two floors of her house. On the smooth marble floor it travels far before stopping; on the rough stone floor it stops much sooner.
Which row correctly describes the friction acting on the moving tiffin box and the reason the rough stone floor stops it sooner?

options.text: friction opposes the motion; the rough surface has more irregularities that grip the box and increase friction
friction helps the motion; the rough surface pushes the box forward more strongly
friction acts only after the box stops; the rough surface holds the box still once it has stopped
friction opposes the motion; friction is the same on both floors, so the box stops sooner only because of gravity

teacher.key_rationale: Friction between surfaces in contact opposes motion, and rougher surfaces have greater irregularities, producing larger friction that slows the box faster — option A. B reverses the direction of friction, C claims friction appears only after stopping, D denies the role of surface roughness.
